title: Degreewise exchange compatibility with a morphism of squares and coefficients
statement:
Let $X_0,Y_0,S_0,T_0,X_1,Y_1,S_1,T_1$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $h_b:Y_b\to X_b$, $e_b:Y_b\to T_b$, $f_b:X_b\to S_b$, $g_b:T_b\to S_b$ for $b=0,1$, satisfying $f_bh_b=g_be_b$. Give morphisms $x:X_1\to X_0$, $y:Y_1\to Y_0$, $s:S_1\to S_0$, $a:T_1\to T_0$ satisfying $f_0x=sf_1$, $g_0a=sg_1$, $h_0y=xh_1$, and $e_0y=ae_1$.
Suppose the two squares $f_bh_b=g_be_b$ are cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]; the comparison faces need only commute. Let $F_0$ and $F_1$ be abelian sheaves on $(T_0)_{\Et}$ and $(T_1)_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], let $\phi:a^{-1}F_0\to F_1$ be any morphism, and let $q\geq0$. For any commutative face use the degree-$q$ exchange obtained from the bounded below derived mate [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange] applied to the coefficient sheaf in degree zero, using the natural exact-inverse-image cohomology identifications [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Higher direct images mean $R^qu_*G=\mathcal H^q(Ru_*G[0])$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Let $P^q_{F_0}:s^{-1}R^qg_{0,*}F_0\to R^qg_{1,*}a^{-1}F_0$ and $Q^q_{e_0^{-1}F_0}:x^{-1}R^qh_{0,*}e_0^{-1}F_0\to R^qh_{1,*}y^{-1}e_0^{-1}F_0$ be the comparison-face exchanges. Let $\beta_{b,G}:f_b^{-1}R^qg_{b,*}G\to R^qh_{b,*}e_b^{-1}G$ be the usual higher-direct-image base-change map [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology]. Define
$$ U_\phi=f_1^{-1}(R^qg_{1,*}\phi)\circ f_1^{-1}P^q_{F_0}:x^{-1}f_0^{-1}R^qg_{0,*}F_0\longrightarrow f_1^{-1}R^qg_{1,*}F_1, $$
$$ V_\phi=R^qh_{1,*}(e_1^{-1}\phi)\circ R^qh_{1,*}(\chi_{F_0})\circ Q^q_{e_0^{-1}F_0}:x^{-1}R^qh_{0,*}e_0^{-1}F_0\longrightarrow R^qh_{1,*}e_1^{-1}F_1, $$
where $\chi:y^{-1}e_0^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}e_1^{-1}a^{-1}$ and the identification $x^{-1}f_0^{-1}\cong f_1^{-1}s^{-1}$ in $U_\phi$ are the canonical inverse-image composition comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. Then
$$ \beta_{1,F_1}\circ U_\phi=V_\phi\circ x^{-1}\beta_{0,F_0}. $$
Neither $\phi$ nor the comparison-face exchanges are required to be isomorphisms. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, affineness or torsion assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Derive the needed derived cube identity directly from horizontal pasting [lemma-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-coherence]. Form the two outer horizontal composites, apply derivedBaseChangeMapPlus_paste_horiz to each at F₀[0], and identify the outer squares using sqf.w and sqe.w. Transport along these equalities by equality elimination; the commutativity witnesses agree by proof irrelevance. Precompose and postcompose with the inverse-image composition isomorphisms, and cancel adjacent inverse pairs. Equality elimination for upperStarCompDerivedPlus expresses both resulting comparisons using the common composite. This is the already proved cube-pasting calculation in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.AbelianExchangeCubeComparisons, reproduced as proved private helpers to avoid importing its unrelated declarations.

proof.text: Use [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange] naturality at the composite a⁻¹(F₀[0]) → (a⁻¹F₀)[0] → F₁[0]. Postcompose the derived cube equality with Rh₁,* of its inverse image under e₁ and the e₁ inverse-image/single-complex comparison. Apply naturality of that comparison to φ. Compatibility of exact-functor localization with single complexes identifies the target composition comparison with the single-complex image of the ordinary square comparison for sqe. Naturality of the exchange for sqh moves the e₀ single-complex comparison to the preceding factor. These operations use no invertibility of φ or of exchange.

proof.text: Prove the exact inverse-image/cohomology composition compatibility needed here explicitly. For a short complex, compare the once-mapped and twice-mapped left homology data using identity maps on kernel and homology objects and the uniqueness of left homology map data. This proves composition compatibility of the canonical homology isomorphisms on complexes [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Descend to derived categories by natural-transformation extensionality along localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], using the factorization equation of the derived composition isomorphism. Restrict to bounded below categories. Combine this with naturality under an isomorphism of exact functors to obtain compatibility for upperStarCompDerivedPlus. Apply it twice and cancel inverse comparisons to get the square comparison for sqf. The parallel single-complex calculation follows by the same localization factorization and restriction to bounded below categories.

proof.text: Apply degree-q homology to the derived equality from step 2, and precompose with the x and f₀ exact-inverse-image/cohomology comparisons. Expand abelianHigherExchange, which is by definition the cohomology of the commutative derived mate. Naturality of the f₁ and x cohomology comparisons and the sqf compatibility from step 3 identify the two sides with the displayed statement. Functoriality identifies the coefficient maps with the homology of derived direct-image maps [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. No separate identification with the resolution-model higher base-change map is required for this Lean statement.

It is exactly what 0ezt uses, with the transition cube and the projection cube and a coefficient morphism that need not be invertible. I tested it on q=0, on the all-identity cube, on phi=0, and on F_0=0 or F_1=0, and it holds in each case. It is not a restatement of the derived cube. Steps 1 to 3 are correct: the cube is applied with its exact face equalities, step 2 is plain naturality, and step 3 makes the cohomology identification natural through localization (2) and (3) and composition clause (2). C4/E5 fault in step 4, fixed: the step applied lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology, which is about Ex_square from def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange, to the cube's E_b, which are commutative-square mates. It never said why the two are the same. I added that argument. theta_square is c^{-1}∘c along fg'=gf' (blueprint_update of def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square, and lem-weil-pbc-square-iso-pasting). Its derived class therefore equals the commutative theta by composition clause (2) and localization (3), and the mates of equal isomorphisms are equal. This is the same repair made to lem-kun-0eym step 5. I added the matching uses and proof_deps. I also declared the tool use lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition, which was off-route and undeclared.
